findings.title: Double-checked locking pattern is incomplete, causing redundant work under concurrent cold-cache access
findings.body: After acquiring the write lock at line 48, the code does not re-check `entryPointAssetsCache` before proceeding to re-read/parse the manifest file. If multiple goroutines call `GetWebAssets` concurrently while the cache is empty (e.g., at startup) and `cfg.Env != setting.Dev`, each goroutine will serialize on the write lock but still redundantly re-read and re-parse the assets manifest (or hit the CDN) instead of reusing the result already computed by the first goroutine. This isn't a correctness bug (the lock does prevent the data race), but it defeats the purpose of caching under concurrent first-access and should re-check `entryPointAssetsCache != nil` right after acquiring the write lock to return early.

findings.title: No test added to verify the data race fix
findings.body: The PR fixes a data race on the global `entryPointAssetsCache` variable by introducing `entryPointAssetsCacheMu`, but no test (e.g., one exercised with `go test -race` under concurrent calls to `GetWebAssets`) was added to validate the fix or guard against regressions. Without such a test, a future refactor could reintroduce the race undetected by CI unless the race detector happens to catch it in another path.
